title: Put SoCs on a board
lede: Write a system manifest that places one or more SoCs on a Nexys Video, sets their clocks and connects their signals to board pins, then program the board and upload a program to each SoC.
prerequisites: A SoC manifest and a working compiler, as in [Build a SoC and run a program on it](#/tutorials/instantiate-core).
A Nexys Video, and Vivado with Artix-7 support.
outcome: A system manifest with one or more SoCs running programs on the board.

stages.title: Create the system manifest
stages.text: A system manifest lists each SoC, the clock it runs on and the board pins its signals use. Start with one SoC.

stages.title: Connect signals to board pins
stages.text: Each line under `[board.pins]` names a board resource and the SoC signal it carries. Move GPIO from the LEDs to a PMOD connector to see how one edit changes the wiring.

stages.title: Set the CPU clock
stages.text: The CPU clock is one number in `[clocks]`. The board can generate only certain frequencies, and the design must pass timing at the one you ask for.

guide.section: 2. Handle a clock or timing failure

stages.title: Build and program the board
stages.text: Check and lint the system first, since both are fast; then build the bitstream and program the FPGA.

stages.title: Add a second SoC
stages.text: A second SoC is a second entry in the system manifest. The two SoCs share no memory. A UART bridge lets both use the one USB serial cable.

stages.title: Upload a program to each SoC
stages.text: Export the software target for each SoC, build a program against it and upload. With a bridge, the upload command names the SoC to load.
